rationale: The 90% claim is deliberately unverified. A statistical chart would lend it false authority; the four evidence-test cards already provide the checking scaffold.
The lesson infers the importance of good character from the hadith. Drawing a literal weighing scale would literalize a religious image rather than teach the intended inference.
The task connects pride, spoken rhythm and declarative style. No complete verse or metric scan is supplied here; a generic desert or poet portrait would not explain those relationships.
The paired terms for separation and companionship already have glosses. A farewell scene would select characters and a setting absent from the supplied passage and would not explain lexical choice.

The modelling already explicitly connects wartime hunger, the night kitchen and the wife sharing bread. A scene would restate the disclosed inference and invent the characters appearance; the bread alone would not teach implicit meaning.
The lamp is a clue to viewpoint, but no specific lamp description or placement is given. An arbitrary lamp photo would turn a textual detail into decoration rather than show who sees it.

The autobiography task asks pupils to locate first person, true events and reflection themselves. No event sequence is supplied for a useful timeline; inventing one would do their comparison for them.
New s6d shows reference and object beams overlapping on a recording plate; explicitly simplified with lenses omitted; scientific basis checked against Georgia State HyperPhysics.
New s6p shows genuine seed-sample containers in Svalbard, labelled as an additional example rather than an assumed location in the reading.

Pupils classify the authors story, statistic and quotation and assess persuasion. No actual items are reproduced here; three generic icons would repeat the named categories without providing evidence.

The listening task evaluates competing arguments, not the literal six qualities. No attributed audio claims are transcribed in the modelling slide; an illustrated list would invent the unheard content.
The ten-step listening topic is used to compare opinions. The deck supplies no actual ten-step sequence, so a flowchart would fabricate the source rather than support listening.

The proverb-presentation task leaves the proverb to the speaker. A preselected proverb scene would narrow that choice; the existing opening-example-conclusion model already teaches delivery structure.
The question about reading as therapy needs an argued oral response. An image of a happy reader would imply the answer instead of helping students support their opinion.
The analytical-essay model already identifies idea, evidence, links and conclusion. An additional sequence would duplicate those explicit writing steps, not add a new relation or concrete source.

Students may choose a writers biography or their own literary experience. A supplied plot arc would choose events for them; the existing beginning-conflict-resolution-ending scaffold preserves that choice.
Five intensive adjective patterns are paired with examples, and alim versus allam is explicitly contrasted. Additional pattern cards would repeat the existing comparison without adding a relation.

The source already pairs morphological patterns with examples and contrasts enduring karim with eventive mukrim. A person illustration could not establish grammatical permanence and would obscure the linguistic evidence.

The earth laughing with flowers is already unpacked as personification with the omitted human and clue identified. A literal smiling earth would encourage a false literal reading; a second text diagram would repeat that analysis.
The synthesis task asks learners to build an idea-evidence-viewpoint table from three sources. Supplying a filled table without those sources would invent positions and remove the synthesis task.
The verse analysis names oath and emphasis particles. A pen photo would not explain the grammatical emphasis, and another labelled verse would merely repeat the existing explanation.
The spring clothing metaphor is already interpreted. A woman-earth composite would literalize the metaphor; the full poem needed for a useful image-to-line comparison is not present.
The lesson compares two literary quotations about the book as a companion. A book-and-person scene would add no evidence beyond the quotations and would fix an interpretation students should discuss.
New s6d shows only the source-deck grounded present scent triggering the grandmother memory; no invented return-to-present plot step.
The cardboard box is an unspecified symbol in very short fiction. A box picture would not teach compression or irony, and a filled plot diagram would disclose a story the deck does not reproduce.

The transformation into a tiger is already described as a symbol of pride. A literal tiger panel would reinforce the surface event, not the authors position; an illustrated transformation would add invented character details.
The central contrast is autobiographical self written as the third-person boy. A portrait would not show narrative distance; the existing explicit pronoun explanation is the relevant scaffold.
The source names UAE innovation examples but asks students to evaluate the article arguments. A building photo would be a proxy for innovation, not evidence for the innovation-or-decline claim.
The distinction is realistic self-worth versus inflated self-worth. Facial expressions cannot establish that mental distinction; the deck gives definitions and asks for two textual proofs.

The creativity listening task compares evidence behind opinions. No specific speaker claims are supplied here, so any illustrated creativity tips would replace rather than support the listening evidence.
The sleep-related listening topic uses an argument-comparison scaffold, with no transcript of its advice. A bedtime sequence would invent advice and would not support comparing speakers.
The spoken poetry analysis assesses voice, organization and evidence. A generic spring landscape would distract from oral analysis and provide no link to the absent full poem.
The future-self presentation intentionally leaves aspirations personal. A chosen profession scene would supply a future identity that is the learners own decision.
The social-media debate needs balanced arguments. Generic phone or smile/frown panels would prejudge benefits and harms without adding sourced evidence.
The innovation essay draws evidence from a named article. A ready-made causal chain would write the argument for learners; the source already provides an essay organization and review checklist.
The two-children writing prompt is open-ended, with no fixed faces or setting. An illustration would constrain the sensory details learners are expected to invent.
The confessions-about-reading task depends on personal recollection. A generic reader image would not teach narrative development and would duplicate the book theme.

The exception types already have separate rule cards and a worked incomplete-negative example. A picture of people cannot encode deletion or syntactic case; another rule tree would repeat those distinctions at this stage.

The specialization construction is explicitly parsed with its omitted verb and contrast to vocative. A group portrait would not identify the hidden grammatical governor; the existing worked sentence carries the distinction.
New s6d aligns two opposite word pairs in the existing example; speaker notes identify excerpts rather than presenting the rearrangement as a full verse.

The introduction asks students to examine linear time, flashback and parallel plots in any novel. No selected event list is supplied for an accurate novel timeline; a filled one would pre-empt the unit reading.
The praise poem is studied through shifts among statement, address and exclamation. A leader portrait would identify the subject but would not show those stylistic changes without the full verses.
The door represents loss and repetition sustains grief. A literal door photograph would privilege the object over the symbolic reading and would not represent the sound pattern.
The biography links pearl-diving hardship to poetry. A generic dhow image would repeat maritime context without showing the textual influence; there is no dated biographical sequence for a timeline.
New s6d separates spoken dialogue above the surface from inferred loneliness and war below, explicitly labelled as a metaphor without measured proportions.
Nature examples are an ant and river, but the inferred lessons are not reproduced. An ant or river panel would repeat nouns rather than show the argument students must retrieve from each paragraph.
Students infer why the author wrote and how writing helped him. The specific experience is not supplied here, so a rescue illustration would invent a literal event and misread the figurative title.
New s6d compares numeral forms and equal value, without any historical chronology or invented dates.
The teacher-replacement statement is a claim to challenge, not a fact. A robot-teacher illustration would legitimize that claim; the deck instead asks for evidence and other sources.

The insomnia listening task contains no reproduced advice or diagnostic content. An illustrated sleep routine would introduce unsupported health recommendations rather than support argument evaluation.
The literature presentation allows any Arab or international writer. A selected author portrait would arbitrarily choose the learners subject and would not teach informed questions and answers.
The essay requires evidence from a biography, sayings and poem about Sheikh Zayed. A portrait would not supply that evidence and would duplicate the named subject rather than the argumentative skill.

The letter addresses a writer chosen for a personal influence. A sample illustrated letter would select an addressee or book not grounded in this prompt; the existing planning checklist preserves the task.
New s6d branches the existing katabtuhu example into verb, subject pronoun and object pronoun, making word segmentation and syntactic role visible.

Fronting the prepositional phrase is already shown with a contrastive worked sentence. A scene cannot encode emphasis, and a second before/after wording panel would repeat the explicit production example.
The opening asks for predictions from the title. A fishing struggle picture would reveal the expected conflict before students form their own prediction.

The Santiago-Manolin relationship is interpreted through loyalty and others judgments. Invented faces or costumes would add ungrounded details; the four source cards already isolate character, relationship and setting.
The departure lesson asks what happens next and why the risk is taken. A scene showing the catch would spoil that prediction, while a generic boat picture would not explain motivation.
External fish conflict, pain and self-doubt are already separate analytical cards. A combat image could show only the external action and would obscure the key internal conflicts.

The present pain and remembered arm-wrestling are already explicitly contrasted. A literal sports image would not explain narrative time; the flashback diagram is being piloted on the simpler thyme example instead of repeating it throughout the unit.
Students are asked what sea, marlin, lions and sharks signify beyond the literal. A picture-to-meaning panel would supply the exact symbolic answers and remove the interpretive step.

The source already gives the catch-attack-resistance-loss sequence. A fully drawn plot curve would supply the climax interpretation pupils are asked to justify, while a shark image would merely repeat the event.
The skeleton and final lion dream are evidence learners interpret. An illustrated ending would foreground the answer and invent visual details, not explain the literary evidence.

The distinction between bodily destruction and undefeated spirit is explicitly explained. A broken body or heroic figure would be both reductive and unsuitable as a literal depiction of the quotation.
The task is to build the novel timeline and place flashbacks. A completed event map would do the assessed organizing work; the existing blank planning instructions preserve that task.

The comparison asks pupils to fill sea, human, conflict and value for Hemingway and Al Jamri. A completed comparison image would supply their textual findings; generic sea photos cannot show individual versus collective experience.
The final project permits diary, letter, critique or film. Illustrating one route would favor that medium; the existing choose-plan-write-review-present sequence supports all options.

Column opinion and field investigation already have contrasting definitions. A newspaper photo cannot show sourcing depth; a filled comparison would merely restate those cards without actual articles.

Students infer social values from commands, prohibitions and reasons in Quranic verses. No full selected verse is supplied here for annotation; a literal light picture would confuse the rhetorical image with the task.
The friendship lesson connects conditional alternatives to sincerity. No complete conditional verse is shown for a reliable branch diagram, and a friendship scene would not encode the grammar.
The central image is the poet imagining his own death and mourners. A literal grave illustration would invent details and add distress without explaining the sound and emotional choices.
The task intentionally asks students to choose a look, word or movement from Mahfouz and infer character. An invented scene or selected detail would do that evidence-selection task for them.
Glasses stand for ways of seeing the world, not just corrected eyesight. An eyeglasses photo would repeat the literal object and fail to show the character change the student must infer.
The Eid memoir asks students to assemble details of old Sharjah from houses, market, clothes and food. A generic heritage scene would conflate unspecified details and pre-empt that reconstruction.

The lesson classifies nutrition, medicine and environment terms and compares paragraph depth. Vegetable or forest photos could not demonstrate paragraph development and would add causal health implications absent from its evidence.

The mirror metaphor develops from culture to thinking to identity. A literal mirror adds no explanatory value; another word sequence would duplicate the explicitly stated progression rather than show new evidence.
The school-rules listening task compares arguments. The actual rules are not transcribed in this modelling slide, so an illustrated rule list would invent the listening source.

The Arab Einstein listening task evaluates tone, pace and pauses, not appearance. A physicist portrait would not support those auditory distinctions, and identity is not specified in the modelling text.
The elegy presentation assesses delivery and supported analysis. A death scene would literalize the poem and distract from the students voice; full verses are absent for rhythmic annotation.
The life-goal presentation leaves the goal personal. A career image would choose a future for the learner, while the existing opening-example-conclusion scaffold supports any goal.

The persuasive calligraphy talk leaves the speaker free to choose a work and evidence. A supplied decorative sample without a chosen claim would narrow that choice rather than teach persuasion; the opening-example-conclusion model already supports a visual brought by the speaker.
The Eid presentation spans world cultures without choosing countries or customs. A montage would introduce unverified practices and narrow the research choices the speaker should make.
The chapter-summary presentation leaves the book open. A preselected book image or plot map would impose content and not teach compression or audience awareness.
The character essay requires evidence from Haditha. A character portrait would invent appearance; a completed evidence chart would supply conclusions students must justify from the story.
The life-goal writing prompt is personal and audience-aware. An aspirational scene would supply the students chosen central idea instead of teaching its organization.
The childhood-memory task asks for sensory detail and flashback from personal life. A fixed childhood scene would constrain the details and sequence students are asked to recall.
The derivative review already pairs forms with examples and parses sabur, muallim and mujtahidin. More pattern boxes would repeat existing classification without adding a new relation.
The same derived form can name a place or a passive entity depending on context. A hospital picture would imply one meaning and obscure the contextual distinction the worked example teaches.

The comparison lesson contrasts direct afal formation with more plus a verbal noun. A size picture would cover only one concrete adjective and would not establish the morphological conditions already listed.
New s6d pairs literal key and washing-machine drawings with source-deck instrument names and morphological patterns.

The nisba model already shows deletions and the added doubled ya. Adding another sequence would repeat it; the potentially unusual place-derived example should not be amplified into a new diagram without linguistic verification.
New s6d compares two whole arrangements: dust with bright moving swords and night with falling stars. Original schematic, no battle attribution or injuries.

The distinction allows a literal meaning in kinaya but forbids it in metaphor through a clue. A sleeping woman or ash pile would illustrate only the surface and encourage a narrow literal interpretation.
Students compare presentation styles and judge evidence across two texts. No complete texts or actual evidence are supplied to populate a meaningful comparison graphic.
New s6d organizes the source-deck four categories by knowledge and wealth with row and column headings, without chronology.
The poetry dialogue reveals pride versus longing. A prisoner scene would add costume and setting absent from the quoted material, and would not teach turn-taking without full lines.
The palace question is rhetorical and challenges arrogance. A palace photo would reinforce wealth as the subject instead of showing why the question does not request an answer.

Clothes on a line are deliberately read as clues to households. An illustrated baby shirt and black robe would supply the exact inferences already given rather than develop evidence-led interpretation.

The memory lesson asks students to reconstruct Awsha through descriptions of her features and home. No actual appearance details are supplied; an illustration would invent the character rather than teach descriptive evidence.

The biography links a nineteenth-century ruler to historical context but gives no dated events. A timeline or portrait would require external identity verification and add little to the contextual inference task.
Students sort logical evidence and emotional appeal in an article about Nabati poetry. A heritage image would itself be emotional appeal, not evidence for how the article is built.

The nature-and-stress question requires combining explanation, numbers and experience. No study values are supplied, so a graph would invent data and a calming landscape would imply the result before evaluation.

The plastic article is studied through links among paragraphs and a student-sourced current statistic. A pollution photo would illustrate the topic without teaching cohesion; no verified data are supplied for a chart.
Time-management listening evaluates opinions with reasons. No schedule or time allocations appear in the model, so an illustrated timetable would fabricate the source.
The thirteen-habits listening topic gives no actual habit list. Pictures would invent or prematurely reveal the content instead of supporting argument evaluation.
The Abu Dhabi presentation is an open historical/current comparison. A landmark photo would select one argument without its evidence and would not teach voice, organization and interaction.
The reading-persuasion talk needs claims and supporting examples. A happy reader would imply the conclusion without adding an argument, and repeat the topic rather than the oral skill.
The alternate-narrator task deliberately leaves the scene and viewpoint to students. An illustrated scene would constrain that rewriting and invent details not supplied here.
The old-home description depends on the learners own sensory memories. A generic heritage interior would overwrite that personal reference and supply the details they must choose.
Approach, hope and beginning verbs are already separated by meaning with a worked syntactic example and a note on an. A generic timeline would misrepresent hope as certain future occurrence.
Vocative categories already have distinct examples and a parsed construct phrase. Person illustrations could not distinguish intended indefinite from proper noun and would add no syntactic evidence.
New s6d highlights half of a whole and pairs it with the existing grammatical example, explicitly labelled as a model rather than a particular book.
The implied-simile proof uses a dead person not feeling a wound. Literal imagery would be distressing and would not teach the inferential argument; the verbal analysis already names the two domains.

The novel-analysis introduction asks about idea, growth and nature description. A completed map would answer those open questions before reading, while decorative landscape would not establish the literary relations.
The national-address poem connects vocative, reminder and imperative to emotion. A national symbol would identify the topic but not show stylistic changes without the actual verses.
Human capability is studied through author evidence and terminology. No study results or concrete mechanism are supplied, so a causal diagram would imply unsupported effectiveness.
Walking benefits must be evaluated against study source and sample. A health-benefit picture would grant those claims authority, and no numerical results exist here for an accurate evidence chart.
The gratitude listening topic does not reproduce its nine effects. Illustrating them would invent health or emotional claims and bypass the listening comparison.
The altruism discussion needs participants own examples and responses. A selected helping scene would choose one moral interpretation instead of supporting open discussion.
The success essay asks learners to organize their own persuasive means. A ready-made success ladder would supply unsourced advice and duplicate the writing process already modelled.
Interrogative versus exclamatory kam already has contrasting case-marked examples. A question/exclamation icon would repeat punctuation, not show the grammatical distinction.
New s6d branches the same word maghrib into prayer and country meanings, clarifying identical form with distinct contextual meanings.
The Anne introduction asks predictions from contents. A plot montage would reveal the development that students should predict; the reading-journal scaffold already offers a drawing option.
Expected boy versus arriving girl is the central opening surprise. An arrival illustration would answer the contrast before the reading and invent costume and faces.
Annes imagined place names reveal her inner world. A fixed landscape image would replace the imaginative transformation the learner is asked to infer from language.
Students build a character-trait-evidence table across chapters for Marilla and Matthew. A completed relationship graphic would supply their findings instead of requiring textual proof.

The friendship lesson traces a test and reunion but leaves the exact event to textual reading. A scene would add ungrounded details and a completed chain would duplicate the existing abstract sequence.
Students must identify an error, its result and learning. No specific error is supplied here; an illustration would invent the example and do the evidence-selection work.
The school rivalry changes to respect, and pupils rewrite the event from Gilbert. A fixed image would privilege one perspective and pre-empt their alternative narration.
The nature-as-inner-state relation depends on textual comparison of happy and sad descriptions. Stock sunny/rainy scenes would imply a fixed weather code absent from the actual passages.
The loss and decision constitute a major ending development. A plotted transformation graphic would make the interpretive conclusion and ending salient before students justify them.
Students choose a theme and collect three pieces of evidence from different chapters. A filled thematic map would provide the target answer and remove that collection task.
The group newsletter allows division of roles and a chosen design. A predesigned page would constrain their design task; the existing named sections already provide a planning scaffold.
The final project permits diary, letter, critique or illustrated talk. A visual model of one option would privilege a medium and reduce the open format choice.
The interview comparison requires ideas, evidence and credibility from two real interviews. No interview claims are reproduced for a filled comparison; a microphone photo would not teach credibility.
Light and darkness are explicitly interpreted as guidance and error. A literal beam or dark-room scene would confuse that figurative analysis, while a second text panel would repeat the explanation.
The Mutanabbi introduction links one life relationship to praise and pride but gives no dated event sequence. An invented portrait or travel map would not explain the selected poetic features.

The distinction is inner rhythm from repetition versus outer meter and rhyme. A sleep or music image would not demonstrate either; no full verse or verified scansion is supplied for rhythmic annotation.

Students select a descriptive verse and identify sense and rhetorical technique. An arbitrary pool scene would choose visual details before that evidence-based reading, with no full verse to constrain depiction.

The literary/historical comparison needs two accounts of the same period. No matched passages or dated events are supplied, so a timeline or portrait would introduce facts rather than compare the writing.
The exclamation-mark title asks students to discover what merits surprise in the story. A punctuation icon would duplicate the title, and an illustrated surprise would supply an ungrounded answer.
The narrative-technique comparison leaves the second writer and passages open. A portrait of one poet would identify a subject but not show how narration, description and dialogue differ.
Added a present-centred map of memory and wish, explicitly not the chronology of story events.

The lesson already names walking space, greenery, social contact and mental wellbeing. A generic ideal-city scene cannot show the expansion of a term; another labelled chain would duplicate the existing modelling explanation.

The astronomy task combines history, astronomical images and number graphics. No star-count data or named object is supplied for a chart; a space photo would illustrate only one medium without teaching synthesis.
The self-knowledge listening task compares speaker arguments. No personality traits or test results are transcribed, so visual types would invent content and bias self-description.
The visits-and-correspondence talk invites the learners own reasons. A selected social scene would imply one reason rather than support organizing their evidence and interacting with listeners.
The intrusive-person talk calls for tactful personal examples. A caricature would stereotype a person and would not teach evidence-led oral structure.
The beloved-city talk deliberately leaves the city personal. A supplied skyline would choose the learners subject instead of supporting the open presentation task.
The technology-impact talk does not select a technology or claim. A gadget montage would be generic proxies and introduce benefits without the speakers evidence.
The literary response lets learners choose between two poems and connect techniques to personal response. A scene would fix an interpretation rather than help students cite their selected text.
The short-story writing task leaves characters, setting and plot open. An illustration would constrain the sensory and figurative choices students are expected to make.
The persuasive writing task allows either city humanization or technology. A supplied conclusion graphic would choose a stance and repeat the organization already modelled.

The derivative-governance lesson already parses the subject governed by a participle and passive subject governed by a passive participle. Another arrowed sentence would repeat those exact analyses without new evidence.
Praise/blame components already have distinct cards and a fully parsed example. A person or thumbs-up image would identify sentiment, not the postposed grammatical specific term.
The exclamatory forms and indirect formation already have case-marked examples. An amazed face would repeat the communicative function while leaving the syntactic distinction unexplained.
Added near/far meaning branches for the exact example al-qusur, with context-based interpretation retained.
The depth comparison requires two actual text arguments. A shallow/deep water picture would literalize the evaluation metaphor; no source evidence is supplied for a filled table.

The lost-and-found story in the hadith already has an explicit event sequence and stated comparison. A desert/camel picture would merely repeat nouns; a divine emotion must not be visually personified.
Andalusian poetry includes nature, city elegy and eastern longing. A palace photograph would cover a setting, not explain all poetic features, while no specific passage constrains a scene.
Added an ordered vertical form diagram with recurring blue rhyme and distinct changing rhymes; explicitly not scansion.

The hail-as-scattered-pearls metaphor is already interpreted. Literal pearls falling from a personified sky would choose an image not grounded in a full verse and obscure the difference between natural event and figurative language.
Added a licensed actual samovar photograph, visibly an example, not the story prop. It resolves an unfamiliar concrete object without deciding its literary symbolism.

Classification, stereotype and bias are explained as a conceptual development. Illustrating groups of people risks reinforcing the stereotypes under discussion; another label chain would duplicate the existing account.
The age-based dismissal is explicitly analysed as attacking a person rather than an idea. A face or straw-man image would literalize fallacy names rather than add a new evidence relation.
The stress listening task evaluates advice without reproducing it. A relaxation routine would add unsupported health recommendations and pre-empt the speaker comparison.
The Andalusian-literature presentation leaves the work and claim to the speaker. A selected historical building would not teach supported literary analysis or oral delivery.
The poet presentation allows any Andalusian poet. An invented or unverified portrait would both impose a subject and distract from cited evidence and interaction.
The personal-experience presentation depends on a learner-chosen event that changed an opinion. A fixed scene would supply their personal content instead of teaching organization.
The research paper leaves the issue and sources open. A populated evidence diagram would invent a study or claim; the existing source and organization checklist supports the task.
The student CV task requires their own qualifications. A filled sample could invent achievements and implies a layout outside this imagery task; a generic resume icon adds no instructional relation.

The oath example is already split into particle, object and answer with reinforcement. An image cannot encode the grammatical relation and a second parsing diagram would duplicate the worked analysis.

The conditional example already identifies both jussive verbs and deletion of nun. A success scene would imply causation without showing inflection; another labelled sentence would repeat the case analysis.
The fa-linking lesson lists several alternative triggers. A causal flow would wrongly suggest they occur in sequence; existing separate category cards preserve the alternatives.

The emphasis example mentions angels and Gabriel. Literal depiction would be inappropriate, and a length bar would reduce rhetorical appropriateness to word count rather than the intended distinction.
The novel introduction invites predictions from pen plus named character. An illustrated girl writing would supply an inferred plot before pupils predict and invent appearance.
Learners are asked to draw actual character relationships. No names or relations are supplied here; a filled map would invent the novel network.

The task distinguishes narration order from occurrence order using the novels actual events. No event list is given, so a completed timeline would fabricate content or pre-empt the students ordering work.
Students classify technique in each chosen passage and compare another writer. A generic storyteller scene cannot demonstrate technique distribution without the actual language.
The pen symbolism changes with each appearance and is a target inference. A pen photo would repeat the literal object; a meaning-labelled picture would provide the interpretive answer.
Students draw the plot curve, locate the climax and predict resolution. A completed curve would do that assessed work, and no actual event list constrains one.
The critical response requires choosing a social issue and collecting evidence before inferring author stance. A supplied issue diagram would skip that selection and invent missing evidence.
The project permits critique, alternate ending or visual presentation. A model of one option would narrow medium and content choices; the existing plan-review-present scaffold covers all.
The historical/literary comparison needs matched childhood passages about Sheikh Zayed. A portrait would not reveal factual precision versus narrative feeling, and the passages are not supplied here.
Added paired hemistich versus variable line lengths. Blocks explicitly represent writing shape, not words or metrical feet.
The night is addressed as an emotional companion. A face in the sky would literalize personification; a night photo would not show the address or inner rhythm.
Students select the strongest poetic evidence for one praised trait and link it to history. A portrait or flag would identify the subject but not support that selection.
The child-dog relationship is read for compassion. A staged scene would invent age, setting and action, and could supply a sentimental interpretation before textual evidence is examined.
New s6d shows a hexagonal carbon lattice with atoms at vertices and the existing structure-properties-applications sequence; scientific lattice detail verified with NobelPrize.org.

Students build a scientific report from their chosen sources. A finished report diagram would duplicate the explicit title-question-evidence-conclusion-source structure without adding subject evidence.
The advertising listening task compares arguments; no actual advert or claim is reproduced. A product image would introduce a new advertiser and cannot establish source credibility.
The modern-poet talk leaves the author and work open. A selected portrait would impose content rather than teach organization, evidence and audience response.
The music-and-science talk leaves the scientific relationship unspecified. Notes and lab icons would be decorative proxies, and a waveform would require an actual sound to analyse.
The documentary talk does not choose a film. A still would choose the students source and add licensing and context assumptions without supporting their own analysis.
The response may address either praise poetry or personified night. A supplied scene would fix a response instead of helping students use their selected textual evidence.
The summary task may use a scientific topic or novel chapter. A filled topic map would choose content and reproduce the target summary rather than support accurate compression.
The chapter response asks learners to connect technique and ideas in a selected passage. No chapter evidence is supplied here for an accurate explanatory scene.
The lesson explicitly asks predictions from the real cover of The Falcon. Substituting a generic falcon or invented portrait would replace the evidence students are expected to inspect.
Pupils underline documented facts and artistic additions in actual text. A supplied depiction would blur that boundary without the underlying passages and historical sources.
Childhood councils are connected to later wisdom but no specific event or visual details are supplied. A childhood scene would invent appearance and setting, not evidence that causal link.

The dual biography/national-history timeline is the student task. No dated event set is provided here; filling one would introduce researched content beyond the imagery brief and do the ordering work.
Added a schematic channel/basin/farm distribution network grounded in UNESCO, explicitly no share quantities or portrayal of the fictional event.
The falcon stands for vision, patience and identity. A falcon photograph would repeat the literal subject and not teach how textual evidence supports the leadership metaphor.
The leadership relationship map is an explicit pupil task. Filling family, advisers and partners would supply the answer; no named characters are supplied for a reliable sourced network.
Students draw a challenge-consultation-decision-result chain for each actual situation. A generic second chain would duplicate instructions, while a filled one needs events absent from the model.

The union lesson compares emotion/dialogue with dated documents. A flag image would not show this genre distinction, and a historical event photo requires a matched textual passage for analytical value.
The event-year-trait timeline is the assessed organizing task. A completed map would select the evidence and infer traits for students rather than scaffold their independent collection.

The group newsletter requires students to distribute roles and design sections. A supplied finished page would constrain their design, while the existing named sections already provide the planning scaffold.
The final project allows letter, critique, film or presentation. A visual model for one output would privilege a medium and content choice rather than support all four.
Existing reviewed literal teaching visual on s3; modelling content checked for fit, original wording unchanged.
A named-character space-training scene would add invented likeness and events; astronaut vocabulary already pictured in preceding lesson. Keep textual character/location evidence.
The speaking task asks students for their own dream and model. A stock occupation would prescribe their personal choice; existing delivery prompts remain.
